claim_set.claim_text: Every AI-supported laboratory result that moves toward release, reporting, or downstream reliance as a reportable record MUST map to a recorded result-admissibility decision — the agent, the result artefact, the intended consequential action, and the authority under which it proceeds. Results lacking a recorded admissibility decision are refused at the action-admissibility gate.

Before an AI-supported result proceeds to release it MUST carry recorded ALCOA+ data-integrity attributes (attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate, complete, consistent, enduring, available) and an intact audit trail for the electronic record. A result whose ALCOA+ attributes are missing or whose audit trail is broken is refused.

Every AI-supported result that proceeds toward release MUST emit a signed, replay-derivable provenance pin binding the supporting model and version, the inputs and pinned reference data, the ALCOA+ data-integrity attributes relied on, and the result-admissibility outcome — data-integrity provenance verifiable offline.

An AI-supported result MUST remain advisory and MUST NOT be released as a reportable record until a named human reviewer — a designated laboratory director, authorised signatory, study director, or competent technical reviewer — records release sign-off. Unreviewed AI-driven result releases are refused and routed dual-channel.

KYE governs AI-supported result generation, release-decisioning and data-integrity/replay at the test-result-admissibility boundary and PROVES the basis. KYE does not perform testing, calibrate equipment, run proficiency testing, handle specimens, or judge the analytical validity of a result.
